text:
Anna (PM): Drafting PRD for the Dedicated capacity launch — need concrete SLA targets, throughput sizing, and autoscale requirements. Link to draft: https://rwd.internal/docs/dedicated-prd-draft

Anna (PM): Pilot customer asks: 99.95% availability, tail latency P95 < 120ms (end-to-end) for typical 256-token responses, and a graceful fallback to a lower-cost model when capacity is constrained. Can we capture acceptance criteria + edge cases? :eyes:

Jordan (Engineering): Quick q — P95 120ms is for which token length and model variant? Also are we specifying per-GPU throughput or per-pool?

Anna (PM): P95 target should be specified for 256-token gen, baseline model (fp16). For throughput I think we should commit per-pool (e.g., 8xA100 pool target) and also provide per-GPU estimates for planning.

Sam (SRE): Ops constraints: cold-starts matter. For quantized 13B models cold start is ~18–25s on our infra when layers warm up. Recommend we accept up to 30s cold-start SLO during scale events, and document mitigation (pre-warm, standby nodes). Also call out cross-AZ failover timelines.

Maria (Infra): Autoscaler note: our autoscaler uses GPU util + queue depth. Proposal: scale-up when avg queue depth > 50 requests for a sustained 30s window; scale-down when queue==0 for 5m and GPU util < 25%. Scale actions should finish within 60s (target) for adding nodes, but quantify that in tests.

Kai (ML): Fallback strategy: add two model variants in the pool — "full" (fp16) and "perf" (Q4/4bit). Perf must use identical tokenization and have QA evals showing quality drop <5% on customer eval sets. Routing rule: when P95 or error-rate threshold is hit, route new requests to perf variant until SLOs recover.

Jordan (Engineering): Draft acceptance criteria (suggested):
- SLA: 99.95% monthly availability (excluding scheduled maintenance)
- Latency: P95 < 120ms end-to-end for 256-token responses on full model
- Throughput: pool-level target 200 rps sustained for an 8xA100 pool (document per-GPU assumptions)
- Autoscale: scale-up action completes within 60s of trigger; scale-down safe conditions and cooldowns defined
- Canary: 5% traffic for 24h, automatic rollback if error rate > 1% OR P95 regression > 15%
- Fallback: automatic routing to perf model when SLOs violated; quality regression <5% on evals

Anna (PM): Edge cases to call out in PRD: sustained bursts (>=10x baseline), model OOMs during large context, sticky sessions/KV cache validity after failover, and multi-tenant isolation under noisy neighbors. Need explicit acceptance tests for each.

Sam (SRE): I'll own runbook and test plan: synthetic traffic generator with realistic seq-len distro, chaos tests (kill node, network partition), validate fallback routing, measure cold-starts and cross-AZ recovery. Will add steps and SLIs in the doc.

Maria (Infra): Add pricing/quoting note: dedicated pools must surface per-token unit economics and a throttling policy for overload scenarios (soft vs hard limits). We should include expected billing behavior during canaries and rollbacks.

Jordan (Engineering): Monitoring requirements: per-route latency histograms, token-level cost breakdown, rollout tracing, and an SDK flag to opt-in to dedicated routing for SDK customers. Also need debug endpoints for KV cache inspection.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: PRD draft updated by Anna — https://rwd.internal/docs/dedicated-prd-draft (v2) :white_check_mark:

Anna (PM): Thanks all — I'll fold these acceptance criteria + edge cases into the PRD and ping for formal review. Targeting engineering sign-off by EOD Friday. @Jordan @Sam @Maria please add your test-plan/runbook links into the doc and tag when ready. :pray:
